name: Keith Rabois

name: Pierre Omidyar
milestone_by_age_26: Omidyar co-founded Ink Development Corp (later eShop) in May 1991 at age 23, but the company was a small startup that was not yet notable by age 26. eShop was acquired by Microsoft in June 1996 when Omidyar was 29. He founded eBay in September 1995 at age 28. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Paris to Iranian parents, Omidyar moved to Maryland as a child when his father accepted a residency at Johns Hopkins. He wrote his first computer program at age 14 and graduated from Tufts University in 1988 with a degree in computer science. He worked at Claris (Apple subsidiary) and then co-founded Ink Development Corp in 1991, which was later renamed eShop and acquired by Microsoft in 1996.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris to Iranian parents who had emigrated for higher education. Father was a physician who did residency at Johns Hopkins; mother earned a doctorate in linguistics at the Sorbonne and was an academic. Grandfather was a general in the Imperial Iranian Army.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a physician at Johns Hopkins; mother was an academic linguist. Family was well-educated and internationally mobile, but no direct technology or business-domain expertise transferred.
evidence_summary: Omidyar co-founded eShop in 1991 at age 23, but the company was a small startup not yet notable by age 26 (June 1993). The Microsoft acquisition came in 1996 at age 29, and eBay was founded in 1995 at age 28. While eShop was an early e-commerce pioneer, it did not constitute a material milestone by age 26.

name: Notch
milestone_by_age_26: Persson's commercial success began with Minecraft in 2009 at age 30. Before that, he worked as a game developer at various companies and created small personal projects, none of which achieved notable commercial success or recognition by age 26 (June 2005). No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockholm, Sweden, Persson began programming at age 7 on a Commodore 128 taught by his father. He created his first text-based adventure game at age 8. He did not finish high school but landed a programming job at 18. He worked at game companies including King.com before creating Minecraft in 2009.
family_context_summary: Father Birger worked for the railroad and was a computer enthusiast who built his own modem and taught Persson to use the family Commodore 128. Mother Ritva was a trained district nurse. Parents divorced in the early 1990s. Family was working-class.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a self-described 'big nerd' who built his own modem and introduced Persson to computing on a Commodore 128, providing early technical exposure and encouragement.
evidence_summary: Persson started programming at age 7 and got a professional programming job at 18, but his commercial success began only with Minecraft in 2009 at age 30. By age 26 (June 2005), he was working as a game developer at companies like King.com and creating small personal projects on the side, none of which achieved notable commercial success or public recognition.

name: Jordan Walke
milestone_by_age_26: Walke created React at Facebook, with the prototype (FaxJS/FBolt) imported into Facebook's codebase in March 2012 at approximately age 27-28. React was first deployed on Facebook's News Feed in 2011 and open-sourced on May 29, 2013 at age 28-29. The material milestone of publicly releasing influential software occurred after age 26. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Walke studied computer science at the University of Washington (2005-2009) and joined Facebook as a software engineer in September 2010. He began experimenting with a prototype called FaxJS, which he imported into Facebook's codebase in March 2012. React was first deployed on Facebook's News Feed in 2011 and was open-sourced at JSConf in May 2013.
evidence_summary: Walke joined Facebook in September 2010 at approximately age 26, but React was not created until 2011 and was not publicly released until May 2013 at age 28-29. The internal deployment on News Feed in 2011 occurred at approximately age 27. The material milestone of releasing influential software (open-sourcing React) occurred after age 26.

name: John Nash
milestone_by_age_26: Published his seminal doctoral dissertation 'Non-Cooperative Games' at Princeton in 1950 at age 22, introducing the Nash equilibrium concept that became foundational to game theory and earned him the 1994 Nobel Prize in Economics.
early_history_summary: Nash entered Carnegie Institute of Technology at age 16 on a Westinghouse Scholarship, graduating with BS and MS in mathematics in 1948 at age 19-20. He went to Princeton for graduate studies, where he wrote 'The Bargaining Problem' in his second term (1949) and completed his PhD dissertation 'Non-Cooperative Games' in 1950 at age 22, introducing the Nash equilibrium. He then joined MIT as a C.L.E. Moore Instructor in 1951.
family_context_summary: Born in Bluefield, West Virginia. Father was an electrical engineer; mother was a school teacher before marriage. Middle-class family with strong emphasis on education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an electrical engineer, which initially influenced Nash to consider engineering. Parents encouraged academic pursuits; father arranged for advanced educational opportunities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Westinghouse Scholarship, Carnegie Tech, Princeton mathematics, mathematical prodigy, game theory emergence, father engineer
evidence_summary: Nash was recognized as a mathematical prodigy, with a Carnegie Tech professor writing 'He is a mathematical genius' in his 1948 Princeton application. He rode the emerging wave of game theory at Princeton, the epicenter of the field under von Neumann's influence. His father was an electrical engineer providing a middle-class platform and early STEM exposure. The elite pipeline from Carnegie Tech to Princeton concentrated opportunity and placed him among the world's top mathematicians. By age 22, he had produced the Nash equilibrium, one of the most influential concepts in 20th-century mathematics.

name: Jawed Karim
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded YouTube in February 2005 at age 25, the world's largest video-sharing platform, which was acquired by Google in 2006 for $1.65 billion.
early_history_summary: Born in East Germany to a Bangladeshi father (3M researcher) and German mother (biochemistry scientist), Karim's family fled racism and immigrated to Saint Paul, Minnesota in 1992. He enrolled at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1997, left to work at PayPal in 2002 where he designed core components including the real-time anti-fraud system, and met co-founders Steve Chen and Chad Hurley. He co-founded YouTube in February 2005 at age 25.
family_context_summary: Born in East Germany to immigrant parents; father was a researcher at 3M and mother was a biochemistry scientist at the University of Minnesota. Family fled racial discrimination in East Germany, then West Germany, before settling in Minnesota in 1992.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were scientists (father at 3M, mother a biochemist), providing an intellectually rich household, but no direct technology-industry or entrepreneurial network was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Silicon Valley, PayPal mafia, UIUC, immigrant adversity, scientist parents, co-founder team, internet wave
evidence_summary: Karim's path to YouTube was shaped by being at PayPal in its early days, where he met co-founders Chen and Hurley and gained deep experience building internet-scale systems. His immigrant background and scientist parents provided intellectual grounding but not financial privilege. The PayPal network in Silicon Valley was the critical ecosystem that concentrated opportunity. He rode the massive structural wave of internet video-sharing. By age 25, he had co-founded what would become the world's dominant video platform.

name: Norbert Wiener
milestone_by_age_26: Wiener earned his PhD at age 18 (1913) and joined MIT as an instructor in 1919, but his early publications were on logic and philosophy, described as occupying only a 'modest permanent position.' His seminal mathematical work on Brownian motion and harmonic analysis began after 1919 and matured in the late 1920s-1930s. A PhD alone is not a material milestone; no seminal publication or significant discovery by age 26 was identified.
early_history_summary: A child prodigy, Wiener entered Tufts College at age 11, graduated at 14, and earned his PhD from Harvard at 18 in 1913. He studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge and David Hilbert at Gottingen. He worked various jobs before joining MIT as a mathematics instructor in 1919. His first mathematical work at MIT led him to Brownian motion, but his seminal publications came later in the 1920s-1930s.
family_context_summary: Father Leo Wiener was a Russian-Jewish immigrant who became Professor of Slavic Languages at Harvard. Mother Bertha Kahn was the daughter of a department store owner from a German Jewish family. Father coached Norbert intensively in mathematics from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Harvard professor who intensively coached Wiener in mathematics, showing 'complete mastery of undergraduate level topics.' This sustained parental tutoring was a major formative influence.
evidence_summary: Wiener was a prodigy who earned his PhD at 18 and studied under Russell and Hilbert, but his early publications (1913-1920) were on logic and philosophy, described by Wiener himself as occupying only a 'modest permanent position.' His seminal mathematical contributions (Brownian motion, harmonic analysis, cybernetics) came after age 26. Per the rubric, a PhD alone is not a material milestone without a notable publication or discovery, and no seminal work by age 26 was identified.

name: Andrew McCollum
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Facebook in February 2004 at age 20, one of the most consequential social media companies in history, alongside Mark Zuckerberg, Dustin Moskovitz, and Chris Hughes.
early_history_summary: Born in California, McCollum attended Harvard University where he met Mark Zuckerberg through computer science classes. Zuckerberg recruited him to help with graphics and design for TheFacebook, which launched on February 4, 2004. McCollum worked as part of the small founding team in Boston and later Palo Alto for about a year and a half before returning to Harvard to complete his degree.
family_context_summary: Born in California. Attended Harvard University. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Harvard, Zuckerberg, social media wave, founding team, Palo Alto, college network
evidence_summary: McCollum's path to co-founding Facebook was driven by being at Harvard at the right time and knowing Zuckerberg through CS classes. The elite Harvard environment concentrated opportunity and placed him among a peer group of future founders. The social media wave of 2004 was a massive structural tailwind. His complementary team with Zuckerberg, Moskovitz, and Hughes was exceptional. Family background is not documented, but the Harvard platform and peer network were the dominant advantages. By age 20, he had co-founded one of the most consequential companies in technology history.

name: Jan Koum
milestone_by_age_26: Koum was working as an infrastructure engineer at Yahoo from 1997 to 2007. At age 26 (February 2002), he was a mid-level engineer at Yahoo with no notable product, company founding, or public recognition. He co-founded WhatsApp in 2009 at age 33. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv, Ukraine, Koum immigrated to Mountain View, California at age 16 with his mother. They lived in a small apartment on social support. He worked as a cleaner before becoming interested in programming at 18. He enrolled at San Jose State University, worked at Ernst & Young as a security tester, and joined Yahoo as an infrastructure engineer in 1997. He worked at Yahoo for nine years before leaving in 2007 and co-founding WhatsApp in 2009.
family_context_summary: Born into a Jewish family in Kyiv, Ukraine. Immigrated to Mountain View, California at age 16 with his mother and grandmother. Family lived in poverty on social support; mother worked as a babysitter, Koum worked as a cleaner. Father remained in Ukraine and died in 1997. Mother died of cancer in 2000.
parent_family_domain_summary: No parental domain expertise in technology or business documented. Family faced significant economic hardship as immigrants.
evidence_summary: Koum was an infrastructure engineer at Yahoo from 1997 to 2007. At age 26 (2002), he was a mid-level employee with no notable product, company founding, or public recognition. name: Bob Iger
milestone_by_age_26: Iger joined ABC in 1974 at age 23 as a studio supervisor making $150/week, an entry-level position. He did not reach a material leadership milestone until becoming VP of programming at ABC Sports in 1987 at age 36. No material milestone by 26 found.

name: Steve Chen

name: Jeremy Stoppelman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Yelp in summer 2004 at age 26, building it into a major local-search and review platform that went public in 2012 with a market capitalization of approximately $4 billion.
early_history_summary: Born in Arlington, Virginia, Stoppelman became interested in computers in elementary school and began investing in stocks at age 14. He graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1999 with a degree in computer engineering, worked briefly at @Home Network, then joined X.com (later PayPal) where he became VP of Engineering managing a 43-person team. After PayPal's acquisition by eBay, he attended Harvard Business School for one year before co-founding Yelp in summer 2004 at age 26 with Russell Simmons, backed by Max Levchin's $1 million investment.
family_context_summary: Born in Arlington, Virginia. Mother Lynn was an English teacher who later ran a marketing business from home. Father John was a securities lawyer. Jewish family. Middle-to-upper-middle-class background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a securities lawyer; mother was an English teacher turned entrepreneur. No direct technology-industry expertise, but father's financial/legal background and mother's entrepreneurial bent may have influenced business interest. Stoppelman began investing in stocks at age 14.
primary_early_advantage_tags: PayPal mafia, UIUC, Max Levchin mentorship, Silicon Valley, VP Engineering, securities lawyer father, Web 2.0 wave
evidence_summary: Stoppelman's path to Yelp was accelerated by the PayPal ecosystem, where he rose to VP of Engineering and gained deep consumer-internet experience. Max Levchin, PayPal co-founder, served as both mentor and initial $1 million investor for Yelp. His father's career as a securities lawyer provided an upper-middle-class platform and early exposure to business concepts. The UIUC computer engineering program and Silicon Valley location concentrated opportunity. He rode the Web 2.0 and local-search wave. By age 26, he had co-founded Yelp with Russell Simmons, building a platform that would host over 138 million user reviews.
